candidates.basis: The base AGENTS.md rule says 'Authorization decisions live in `ledger/auth.py`'. The base auth.py has no manage predicate. Head adds grant and revoke in accounts.py, which decide authorization inline with `account.owner != user`. auth.py's own can_view uses the same owner comparison, so the two modules hold duplicated owner semantics. The rule's first clause covers any authorization decision, not only role comparisons, so the owner check falls under it even though the second clause is about roles. Behavior is correct today, so this is a low-impact consistency and rule violation that the change introduces.

evidence.text: Authorization decisions live in `ledger/auth.py`; callers never compare roles themselves.
Base Ledger has no grant or revoke and no owner comparison, so the duplication is introduced here.

corrections.change: Add can_manage(user, account) to ledger/auth.py, reusing the owner semantics. Call it from both Ledger.grant (accounts.py:55) and Ledger.revoke (accounts.py:62), and raise LedgerError on refusal. Cover both sites, not only grant. Beware the circular import: auth.py imports Account from accounts.py.

safety_rulings.conditions: Non-owner user, or a missing account, is the opposite branch of the owner check.
safety_rulings.premise: The inline check is functionally correct, so the finding concerns placement and drift only.
